implementation_notes: kotlinx.html provides both halves directly: the same tag DSL builds a DOM tree on JS/Wasm targets or streams into a Writer/Appendable on the JVM, and the writer you pick is the channel - appendHTML() for HTML, the XHTML/XML writers for machine-readable output - so one page definition serves several channels. Build the page with the DSL and let the writer escape text; unsafe { } is the deliberate escape hatch for sanitised fragments only. Ktor integrates the same builders through respondHtml/respondHtmlTemplate, where templates and placeholders carry the layout and the logical page is the data passed into them. Prefer the DOM form when one page must be inspected or reused before it is written, the writer form when it is consumed once.
pitfalls: The writers escape interpolated text, but unsafe { } disables that for its whole block - inside it a pre-escaped string is a double escape or an XSS hole depending on the channel.
JVM streaming builders write straight into the Appendable, so a failure halfway through leaves a partial response that cannot be replaced by an error page.
The DOM API differs per target (Kotlin/JS document vs JVM Writer), so code shared across targets must stay on the common builder surface.
